protocolMetadata.instructions:
Raylight is a motion design video editor (raylight.app). These tools drive the user's LIVE editor tab: the user watches every edit happen on their canvas in real time.

This server's tools are: get_editor_status, list_projects, file_shared_project, get_editor_capabilities, get_project_overview, get_shot_details, render_stills, render_filmstrip, render_waveform, check_sync, get_design_guide, apply_edits, save_as_video, list_videos, update_share_page, list_templates, start_from_template, get_import_report, get_import_status, discard_import_session, score_import_fidelity, upload_media. A Raylight tool name outside this list does not exist on this server (it will fail with a hint pointing at the nearest real tool).

Workflow: call get_editor_status first. If no tab is connected, give the user the exact project link to open and wait. Once connected, get_project_overview describes the whole project (coordinate system, shots, styleDigest, media). Read a shot with get_shot_details before editing it, make changes with apply_edits, then LOOK at your work with render_stills or render_filmstrip and fix what reads wrong. apply_edits takes up to 200 edits per call and validates each one on its own (a malformed edit fails alone, the rest still run), so create and animate in ONE batch: give a creating op ref: "name" and write "$name" in any id field of a later edit instead of round-tripping ids; every creating result carries a structured created object, and the top level carries refs and createdIds. Batch flags: lint: false skips the composition lint; bypassTasteRules: true skips the taste guards (text stack, camera wobble, text size caps) while hard limits stay, for deliberate cases only. Motion you already have as sampled values (a traced curve, a spring you computed, another tool's output) goes in with set_keyframes and the editor fits the blocks; set the framing a shot opens on with set_camera_rest before adding moves; new frames carry their members through animation (membersFo

tool.name: get_project_overview
tool.title: Read project overview
tool.description: Read the whole project at a glance: the coordinate system and visible canvas bounds in world units (canvasWorldUnits.center + visibleX/visibleY; the center is NOT always (0,0)), every shot with its absolute start/duration and asset list, the styleDigest (every color in use with its roles, every font family with its weights: match these when adding elements so the project stays cohesive), the mediaLibrary (every image/video/audio available to the project: media used in shots plus everything uploaded to the Assets panel, usageCount 0 = uploaded but not yet placed; placeable via add_image/add_shot), savedEasings when the user has saved any (easings they kept from the timeline, applied by name with easingPreset: the count plus the newest few names, or unavailable when the library could not be loaded, which does not mean it is empty), where the user currently is (playhead, current shot, selection), and on projects imported from another app an import block (decision counts, fidelity score, and the renderedLayers that were placed as media because they could not be rebuilt natively, each with its assetId and reason code). A fresh copy of this exact data is already included in the user's message as project_state; call this tool only to RE-read after apply_edits changes the project, never at the start of a run. Pass section: "savedEasings" to get ONLY the user's complete saved easing library instead of the overview (every name, newest first, each with the curve or spring it plays in the form the easing op fields take); use it when the name you need is not among the newest few, or to read a saved curve's values.

tool.name: get_shot_details
tool.title: Read shot details
tool.description: Read one shot in full detail: every asset with transform (world units, degrees), MEASURED rendered footprint (sizeWorld: width/height plus left/right/top/bottom world edges; use these for spacing and overlap math, never guess sizes), lifetime (shot-local ms), entrance/exit, animation blocks, per-kind extras (crop and video trim, enabled layerEffects, frame size/clipContent, containerId = the frame a layer belongs to, icon identity on inserted icons, audio mix, material on extruded layers and bevel on extruded paths), groups with their members, their explicit pivot when one is set (absent = the measured visual center of the members), and group animation blocks, plus camera framings/moves (framings report rollDeg when set), enabled effects, and the key light for the shot (resting pose plus its animation blocks) when it has one. Fields at their rest defaults are OMITTED from asset summaries: no rotationDeg means {0,0,0}, no scale means 1, no opacity means 1, no entrance/exit means type "none", no name means unnamed, no depth on a shape, path, or text layer means flat (depth is reported in world units when the layer is extruded), no material means Matte, no bevel means square depth edges, no light means the shot is unlit, and only enabled effects are listed. Scale animation blocks report amount as amountUnit "multiplierOfRest"; the same multiplier basis add_animation accepts, so a block you wrote as 1.1 reads back as 1.1 and can be passed back to update_animation unchanged. Non-uniform scale reads back as a {x, y, z} object instead of a single number (read-only: update_asset.scale writes a uniform scalar, so adjust size via sizeWorld-aware position/size edits rather than by flattening a non-uniform scale). When the shot has geometric problems, the payload includes lint: findings for layers clipped by the frame edge, buried behind opaque layers in paint order, colliding text, frame members clipped away, near-miss alignment, and cramped gaps; fix warnings before adding anything new. Call this for any shot you intend to edit before editing it.

tool.name: render_stills
tool.title: Render frames
tool.description: SEE your work: renders 1-4 real frames of the final film at the given ABSOLUTE project times and returns them as images. Each frame is the true render the user will see: camera moves, entrance/exit animations mid-flight, animation blocks, effects, background, everything. Use this after apply_edits to review composition, spacing, legibility, and effect intensity with your own eyes, then fix what reads wrong and render once more to confirm. Pick decisive moments: just after entrances settle (shot start + ~700ms), the composed mid-shot hold, just before a cut. To judge motion over time, prefer render_filmstrip. Pass region to ZOOM onto part of the canvas at full resolution: use it to verify small text is legible and details are crisp (region frames render with camera moves suppressed, so also check the real framing without a region). The first content block is a JSON calibration record: with a region it is {regionView: {zoom, center, visibleWorld {minX,minY,maxX,maxY}, imagePx, pxPerWorldAtZ0}} computed from the framing actually rendered (the region is FIT inside the image at the project aspect, so visibleWorld is usually wider or taller than the rect you asked for; never assume pxPerWorld = imagePx.width / region.width), and without a region it is {frameView: {imagePx, canvasWorld, pxPerWorldAtRest}} (exact only while no camera move is active). Each still's label also carries layers: [{assetId, name, kind, px: {x, y, w, h}}], the resting pixel rect of every visible layer in that image (top-left origin, z=0 plane through the camera active at that time), so you can point at what you see. Morphs are the one motion the rects follow: a layer a morph has taken out of the picture at that time (a morph target before the flight lands, a layer after it has become its target) is left out, and a layer a morph is flying or landing is listed where the morph has it, marked morphing: true. A frame with a missing or half-loaded asset means media was still loading; render that time again.

region.description: Optional world-unit rect to zoom onto (clamped to the visible canvas, then FIT at the project aspect, zoom capped at the framer's ceiling). Use an asset's sizeWorld from get_shot_details, padded ~20%, to inspect that layer up close; read the exact visible extent and px/world back from the regionView block.

tool.name: render_filmstrip
tool.title: Render filmstrip
tool.description: SEE MOTION: renders 4, 6, or 9 evenly spaced real frames across a time span and returns them as ONE contact-sheet image (reading order left to right, top to bottom, each tile labeled with its absolute time). This is how you judge animation: whether an entrance cascade actually cascades, whether a camera move eases in, whether elements collide mid-flight, how a cut lands. Span one beat at a time: an entrance (shot start to start + ~1200ms), a camera move, the 600ms around a cut. Use 6 frames by default, 9 for a long or busy span, 4 for a quick check. Tiles are smaller than single stills; for fine detail or small-text legibility follow up with render_stills (optionally with a region).

tool.name: render_waveform
tool.title: Render waveform
tool.description: HEAR your work: renders the real project mix across a time span as a waveform + spectrogram strip (one image, timeline-aligned), with the span's visual beats - cuts, entrances, animation starts - overlaid as numbered markers and listed with absolute times. This is the audio filmstrip: use it after placing sounds to see whether transients land on the markers, whether a music bed leaves room for SFX (spectrogram shows competing energy), whether a sound is present at all, and where dead air sits. The mix is the true export mix: block envelopes, fades, per-layer effects, ducking, everything. Span one moment at a time (the ~1500ms around a cut or entrance) for precise reading, or a whole shot for the energy arc. For exact numeric offsets between sounds and beats, use check_sync; this tool is for seeing the shape.

tool.name: check_sync
tool.title: Check audio sync
tool.description: MEASURE audio-visual sync: detects transient onsets in the real project mix and correlates them with the span's visual beats (cuts, entrances, animation starts). Returns JSON: per beat, the nearest onset and the signed offset in ms (positive = the sound lands LATE, negative = early, null = no sound marks that moment within 250ms), plus unmatched onsets (sounds that mark nothing visual). Use it after sound work to verify hits land where they should, then fix offsets with move_sound (impacts land ON the cut; whooshes typically lead it by ~60-120ms so the energy peak arrives with the visual). Omit startMs/endMs to check the whole timeline. A null onset on a beat you scored means the sound is missing, too quiet, or too soft-attacked to register - render_waveform shows which.

tool.name: get_design_guide
tool.title: Read design guide
tool.description: Raylight's motion design guide, distilled from the official hand-built templates (recreations of top-tier motion design from Linear, Apple, Fey, Revolut and others). Topic "craft-rules" returns the full craft ruleset (identical to the in-app director's brief; skip it if those rules are already in your system prompt). Topic "measured-craft" returns the aggregate timing/text/camera/effects numbers; a template topic returns that template's scene-by-scene beat sheet (exact arrival times, amounts, easings, camera beats, palette) plus preview images. The templates are the ground truth of what looks good: fetch the closest template's topic BEFORE authoring any scene's motion (not just when recreating a known look) and mirror or transplant its beats; its "Scene N" numbering matches apply_template_motion's sceneIndex. tool.name: save_as_video
tool.title: Save design as video
tool.description: Copy the CURRENT project, which must be a design (a still: get_project_overview reports a designSize), into a NEW video project so it can be animated. The layers, lights, effects, and background carry over; the canvas snaps to the nearest video aspect ratio and the camera pulls back if needed so the whole design stays in frame. Returns the new project id and an editUrl. It does NOT open or switch to the new project: give the user the editUrl and keep working in the current project unless they switch. Pass "name" to title it (default: "<design name> (Video)"). Use when the user wants motion on a design; a design itself never plays.

Use it to find the shareId for update_share_page, or to hand the user a link to a video they already exported.

tool.title: Customize share page
tool.description: Customize the user's share page: the Linktree-style page every exported video lands on (their name and avatar, a headline, the video, link buttons, colors). "page" edits the page itself and applies to every video: headline (one line under the name, max 80 chars), links (up to 8 {label, url} buttons; the full list replaces the old one), background and accent (#rrggbb; text color follows the background automatically), backgroundGradient (a gradient over the background color, or null for a flat color: {gradientType: "linear" | "radial" | "angular" | "diamond", angle in degrees where 0 = bottom to top, 90 = left to right, 180 = top to bottom, stops: 2 to 12 of {position 0-1, color #rrggbb}}; when setting one, also set background to its first stop), pattern (a faint repeating texture on top: "none", "dots", "grid", "warp" (a wavy grid symmetric around the middle of the screen), "waves", "mesh", "rings", "ripple", "blobs", "dither", "grain"), buttonStyle ("fill", "outline", "soft"), showDownload, showShareLinks (the copy link, X and LinkedIn buttons under the video), hideBranding (removes the "Made in Raylight" credit; Max plan only. Free pages always show a "Made in Raylight" block with a sign-up button and an end card when the video finishes; Hobby and Pro pages show a small credit in the footer). Free plans can set headline and links only; the other fields answer with an error naming the plan gate, so tell the user instead of retrying. "video" edits one video and needs shareId (from list_videos): title, description (under the video, max 500 chars), cta ({label, url} button above the links, null to remove), allowRemix (lets viewers open a live copy; only shows on a public video made from a project the user owns, video.remixAvailable in the result says whether it is live; turning it off kills the remix link on the page right away), visibility ("public" = anyone with the link can watch, "private" = only the user; ask before making a video public), showViewCount ("everyone" shows the view count on the page, "owner" hides it from visitors). Returns the resulting page. Use when the user asks to brand, personalize, or add links or a call to action to their share link.

page.description: Owner-level page settings; every key optional.

tool.name: upload_media
tool.title: Upload media
tool.description:
Put an image, video, or audio file into the project's asset library so apply_edits can place it (add_image {src}, add_shot {mediaSrc}, set_background {image}, add_sound {mediaSrc}). Use it whenever the user gives you a file or a link to one. Three ways to call it, chosen by which fields you pass:
1. {url}: a direct, publicly reachable link to the file itself (not a page that embeds it). The server fetches it (max 100 MB). This is the usual path.
2. {base64, mime}: the file bytes inline. Small files only (under 5 MB decoded; a data: URL is accepted).
3. {mime, bytes} with no url/base64: for a LOCAL file you can read with a shell but cannot inline. Returns an uploadUrl; PUT the raw bytes to it (curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: <mime>" --upload-file <path> "<uploadUrl>"), then call upload_media again with {assetId} to finish. bytes must be the exact file size; for video over 100 MB also pass durationMs.
Bulk (up to 20 per call, one result per item in input order, one bad item never fails the others): {urls: [{url, name?, mime?}]} fetches several links (way 1) and returns results[]; {files: [{mime, bytes, name?, durationMs?}]} reserves several signed PUT slots (way 3) and returns uploads[] each with assetId + uploadUrl + headers + name; {assetIds: [...]} finishes several signed uploads in one call (safe to retry: already-finished ids return ok). Each item carries ok plus either the asset fields or an error; retry only the failed items.
Supported: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime, audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/mp4, audio/x-m4a, audio/aac. The file is measured (width/height, duration) and appears in the user's Assets panel immediately with an "Add to canvas" toast; the result's src, libraryRef, and name are all accepted by apply_edits. Videos are stored as given (no re-encode): prefer H.264 mp4.

url.description: Way 1: direct public http(s) link to the file.

mime.description: The file's mime type. Required for ways 2 and 3; optional with url. One of: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif, video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime, audio/mpeg, audio/wav, audio/mp4, audio/x-m4a, audio/aac.

name.description: Display name for the asset in the library (defaults to the URL's filename). apply_edits can reference the asset by this name.

urls.description: Bulk way 1: several direct public links fetched in one call. Returns results[] in the same order, each {ok, url, ...asset} or {ok: false, url, error}.

bytes.description: Way 3: exact file size in bytes.

files.description: Bulk way 3: reserve a signed PUT slot per local file in one call. Returns uploads[] in the same order, each {ok, assetId, uploadUrl, headers, name} or {ok: false, name, error}; PUT each file, then finish them all with {assetIds}.

base64.description: Way 2: the file bytes as base64 (small files only).

assetId.description: Way 3, second call: the assetId returned with the uploadUrl, once the PUT has succeeded. Safe to retry.

assetIds.description: Bulk finish: the assetIds from a {files} call once every PUT has succeeded. Returns results[] per id; safe to retry with only the failed ids.

projectId.description: Optional: the project to upload into (ids from list_projects). Omit to use the project open in the user's connected editor tab.

durationMs.description: Way 3, video/audio: duration in ms if known (ffprobe or file metadata). Required for videos too large for the server to measure.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Raylight to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Raylight to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.raylight.app/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Raylight MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Raylight scores 96/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Raylight's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, Raylight scores 77/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 27 of 27 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Raylight?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Raylight in design-creative on the Manufact MCP catalog include Motion, MotionVid, Sleek, Streamloop MCP, and Image Generation.

_published_faq.name: How can Raylight improve its MCP documentation?
